chunks: The venerable Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him):

that he was asked about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'And it was said: Is there a healer?' [75:27]. He said: That is the saying of the son of Adam when death comes to him. He says: 'Is there a doctor? Is there a defender?'
He said: 'And he realizes that it is the parting' [75:28] — meaning, the parting from family and loved ones at that moment.
He said: 'And the legs are joined together' [75:29]. He said: This world and the Hereafter are joined together.
He said: 'To your Lord that day is the driving' [75:30] — to the Lord of the Worlds on that day is the return.

key_terms.الساق بالساق: Literally 'leg upon leg', interpreted by the Imam as the joining/intertwining of this world (dunya) with the Hereafter (akhirah).
key_terms.الفراق: The parting, separation — specifically from family and loved ones at the moment of death.
key_terms.المساق: The driving, being driven — referring to the soul being driven toward God after death.
key_terms.راق: Healer or one who recites ruqyah (spiritual healing). In the Imam's interpretation, it refers to any medical or spiritual healer the dying person calls for.

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of Quran 75:27-30 about the moment of death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) was asked to interpret four consecutive verses from Surah al-Qiyamah (75:27-30) that describe the moments of death. He explained that 'Is there a healer?' refers to the dying person desperately seeking medical help, 'the parting' means departing from family and loved ones, 'the legs being joined' symbolizes the merging of this worldly life with the Hereafter, and 'the driving to your Lord' means the soul's final return to God. This interpretation was delivered in the context of Sheikh al-Saduq's scholarly assembly in Rabi' al-Awwal 368 AH.
